einstellungen.text: Something in this forest copies voices. At midnight, it calls out in the voice of Ben's grandpa. And Ben's grandpa died a year ago.
It's midnight. Mom should be here by now. She isn't.
It's been quiet outside for twenty minutes. That's worse than any clicking.
You're sitting on the couch under a blanket. The flashlight is pointed at the door.
Ben counts the logs by the fireplace. Eleven. He counts them three times.
Then the voice comes from the lake. Calm. A little hoarse.
“Benny! Come on, let's go fishing. The perch are biting.”
Ben freezes. Only one person ever called him Benny.
“We came here every Sunday. To this exact lake.”
Grandpa taught him to swim here. And how to put a worm on a hook without crying.
“He always said: you don't have time. You make time.”
Last summer, Grandpa asked one more time. Ben didn't have time. Practice, friends, whatever.
Two weeks later, Grandpa was in the hospital. Ben meant to call him back. Tomorrow. Then the day after.
“I never called him back.”
On Ben's wrist, Grandpa's old watch is ticking. He hasn't taken it off since the funeral.
You think about Mom. When was the last time you two just hung out? No phones. No rush.
“Benny. I'm waiting.”
Ben gets up. He walks to the door. You grab his sleeve.
“That's not him, Ben.”
“I know. I just wanted to hear him one more time.”
You sit back down. Ben buries his face in the blanket. Outside, it calls three more times. Then silence.
“If we get out of here, I'm calling everyone. Seriously, everyone.”
And suddenly you realize what that means. It knows Grandpa's voice. So it was here last summer too. It was listening.
Who knows how many voices it's collected. Summer after summer.
At twelve forty-seven, Mom texts. A tree is down across the road. She's walking the rest. On foot. Through the forest.
She doesn't know what's waiting out there. You do. You put on your jacket.
